Boreas Is a Rugged Yet Refined Sprinter Camper Van Built for Four-Season Adventures
33 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / White River Overland
Versatility is the name of the game when it comes to camper vans. In my opinion, a proper build will be able to tackle a wide range of scenarios, keeping you comfortable regardless of how you adventure. That's exactly what this camper van can do – meet Boreas.
Boreas is a conversion based on a 2024 AWD Mercedes-Benz Sprinter with a 144" wheelbase. It was created by White River Overland, an Aspen, Colorado-based company specializing in, as it shared, "designing and building semi-custom van conversions, overland vehicles, and truck upgrades engineered for four-season mountain travel."
White River Overland describes Boreas as the "ultimate Colorado rig." To it, that means it can handle things like day-to-day runs on asphalt, skiing adventures, backcountry driving, and more. As always, let's start the tour with the exterior.
The van rides on 17-inch bronze Reika Rambler wheels wrapped in Falken Wildpeak all-terrain tires. To improve the off-road capabilities, the builders installed a Van Compass Stage 4.3 suspension kit, which comes with front and rear Falcon adjustable shocks.
At the back, you'll find a heavy-duty swing-away bike rack and an Owl Vans spare tire carrier/ladder combo. Use it to climb on top of the vehicle and you'll discover a flat-mounted Starlink antenna, a 10-foot Thule awning, and a 225 W solar array. The company also made two cut-outs for a Maxxair vent fan and a Nomadic Cooling A/C unit.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / White River Overland Other notable mods are Owl Vans steps, Rigid scene lights on the sides, an Arctic Tern awning-style window, and flares. Flares, also known as pods or capsules, are designed to increase the van width to allow you to install a bed inside in an east to west arrangement instead of the standard north to south.
This rig's Vanspeed capsules are color matched to the van's body and come with half-slider windows.
Pull on the sliding door's handle, and it will open by itself. Enter, and a well-thought-out interior will greet you. One of the first things you'll notice is the open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space.
The driver and passenger seats are mounted on factory swivel bases, so they can be turned around to face the back of the van. What's more, White River Overland added a Wolfbox Pro G9000 dash cam/digital mirror, as well as a Van Wife Components headliner shelf.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / White River Overland Regarding aesthetics, the customer opted for grey laminated ply cabinetry, grey 2tec2 woven vinyl flooring, and slatted wall panels with a black background.
Straight ahead of the entrance, you'll come across a small bench, which can be described as the continuation of the front seating area. Between the bench and the driver's seat, you'll find a Lagun table mount with a folding top that can be adjusted to be reached from wherever you sit.
The bench integrates a decently sized drawer with a magnetic closure system. Above, you'll find a cabinet next to a touchscreen display for monitoring and controlling the power system.
Next, we have a kitchen, which is split into two units. The one on the passenger side features a deep black stainless steel sink with a retractable faucet, a drawer, and two lower cabinets. On the side of the counter, the builders added a panel with switches for four different lights, as well as one for a water pump.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / White River Overland One of the cabinets hides a Laveo dry-flush toilet on a slide-out. The slide-out is heavy-duty, so it can support the weight of a human – that means you can sit straight down and do your business without having to first remove the toilet.
The unit on the opposite side is meant mostly for storage. It has a fridge with a tiny freezer compartment, a tambour door hiding a pantry, a RecPro microwave oven, and a floor-to-ceiling closet with hanging space.
The rear part of the living space is taken up by, like in most vans, the bedroom. The customer chose a space-maximizing setup with a Murphy bed and abundant storage space.
On the driver's side, White River Overland added the Murphy bed platform, which, during the day or when you don't need the bed, is secured upright.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / White River Overland Setting up the bed is quick and easy – lower the platform, which rests on a unit on the other side, and then unfold a custom mattress made up of multiple pieces. To climb on it, you can use a slide-out step.
The bed platform sits on top of a unit that, besides offering some room to store your items, also accommodates a 48V power system.
Its highlights are a 7.2 kWh capacity and a 3,000 W inverter. Three charging sources are available: solar power, shore power, and DC-DC charging while the engine is running.
As for plumbing, the van is equipped with a 30-gallon (113-liter) freshwater tank, an under-mounted greywater tank, an electric water heater, and an outdoor shower connection.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / White River Overland This part of the van also has four overhead cabinets, a smart TV attached to a swivel mount, and a Maxxair vent fan above.
There's one more important amenity in this rig, one that hides in plain sight: a shower. By the entrance, you can lift a floor mat and reveal a teak shower mat sitting on top of a stainless steel pan. To complete the shower setup, you need to hang a curtain to the ceiling and connect a showerhead to the sink faucet.
All in all, Boreas by White River Overland pairs luxury with ruggedness in an aesthetically pleasing design suitable for a vast range of uses. What's really impressive is the number of comforts it manages to fit despite being built on a short wheelbase Sprinter van.
